title: The Box Within the Cat
text: “That’s missing the whole point…”
“Raph.”
“Demon lords tend to be dragons in the classic template, don’t they. In this world it seems dragons fit that role too. Something about how on Glass’s side, there apparently used to be a demon lord.”
It sounded like Father was relaying something he’d heard from Fan Pig.
“Dragons are supposedly like your subordinates or something—how’s that work? Seems like you were a demon lord yourself at some point too.”
“Same view as yours, though dragons do tend to get called that a lot. Sometimes they take on the role of commanding monsters and disciplining humans or other creatures when they cause trouble.”
“Why’s that?”
“You two should understand, shouldn’t you? Without something to keep things in check, this world risks producing something like the mastermind behind the Waves.”

Is that what he meant earlier when he was going on about order and whatnot? So the Crimson Swine, whose very existence is a plague upon the world, is exactly the sort of thing dragons exist to keep humanity from becoming, I take it?
“Incidentally, because they bear that duty of order, the higher-ranking ones among them can use part of the white magic as breath attacks.”
“White… Gaelion used that. Some oddly white flame-like thing.”
Rival had used that too, indeed. The Dragon King seemed capable of it as well, so… ah, I see, dragons can wield a special sort of magic.
“White magic, was it?”
“Primordial magic. The power of order that upholds set rules. In a dragon’s case, it silences wielders of problematic power and grants supportive effects to nearby allies.”
Oh… Ho-kun really knows his stuff.

“As a contrast, more or less—there’s a foundational magic with the attribute of black. More precisely, it’s ‘the transparent black that has exhaled all things and arrived at nothingness’… a creative force that existed even before the very word ‘nothing’ did.”
As Ho-kun explained this, Ark looked away, I noticed.
“The cat over there knows more about this stuff than I do, though.”
“Well… honestly, that’s not really something I should go teaching you about my power. Though, it acts on things whether you know about it or not.”
“I don’t really get it.”
“You don’t need to. There are also gray-line spells that get us noticed if witnessed, you know.”
“Oh? Such as?”
“Such as… hmm, magic that restores someone to their previous-life form? That one would probably hit hard against reincarnators slipping around in this world.”
Ark asked Ho-kun this.
“Yeah, most of those souls are rotten clean through even before reincarnation, so I doubt they’d want to go back to their old form. Either way their souls are rotten, so.”

“That’s a pretty brutal, hellish spell. Turning someone back into their old form from some dream isekai reincarnation fantasy… wait, does that even apply to us, since we were summoned or transported instead?”
“If we’re talking about stripping away a false skin, no, that wouldn’t apply to you. You two came here as you already were.”
That is indeed true. I don’t entirely fail to understand the desire to become someone else, but I have no wish whatsoever to become like those reincarnator types, I say.
“In the sense of tracing the roots of a soul, if the target’s strength is low enough to escape detection, it might still be usable, I suppose?”
“Well… I guess so? Though I wouldn’t call it a great method.”
“That said, some people don’t even have a previous life. For those, it’d either be meaningless or backfire badly.”
Ark and Ho-kun were deep in some operational discussion that only the two of them could follow, indeed.
“Don’t really get it, but soul roots, huh.”

“Right. For an easy example anyone could follow—take the dragon living in this village. That runaway of ours has roots tracing back to a dragon from a world governed by the sword’s sacred weapon. It’s something you can tell through the soul’s authentication, or rather its structure.”
I had witnessed the male Rival sneaking off to visit Ark and the others whenever Doctor and Father weren’t around. It appeared to be paying respects, more or less.
“Gaelion, huh… so dragons have roots too, and you can tell which world they originally came from.”

“As for the other one—the girl who does that comedy-duo routine with Motoyasu-kun sometimes—that’s a different case. Actually, way back, I once met a distant past life of hers. You could probably check it yourself too, though there’s no need to bother.”
Rival’s backstory is of no interest to me whatsoever, I say.
“The female one too, huh.”

“Well, dragons repeat reincarnation after all. It’s only natural she’d forget. Back then, the reigning Dragon Emperor was her. In this world, two Dragon Emperors are happily squabbling with each other.”
“You said you found that preferable to having power concentrated in one, didn’t you.”
“They’re the younger sister and brother chosen as vassals of the whip, aren’t they? Getting along is a good thing, isn’t it.”

Is this some rivalry between the two Rivals? I do recall them having quite the ferocious spat. Incidentally, thanks to that whole runaway chocolate monster incident, Father has decided to stay well out of it.
“Reincarnation, huh…”
“Curious about its purpose?”
Right as Father muttered that, Ho-kun tilted his head slightly and asked.
“The way you two talk about it, it sounds like some ritual performed to keep souls from rotting.”
“That’s one facet of it, sure.”

“Though it varies depending on the world’s principles. In some places, the goal is to break free from the wheel of reincarnation entirely and achieve liberation. Other places get the concept twisted and end up rotting souls instead. True liberation is difficult, you know.”
“Given the scale you’re talking, you two probably even know the very reason worlds exist in the first place.”

“I wouldn’t claim to be that arrogant. Everything in existence is emptiness is form, form is emptiness… Chasing only after meaning makes it all so dull, doesn’t it? Always changing—stagnation is where decay begins.”
And at that, I felt Ark let out something like a dry laugh.
“I get that Ho’s that kind of bird, but you, Ark—I really don’t get you at all. Are you supposed to have been a demon lord or not?”
“Now, I wonder?”
Ark dodged the question again, indeed. Father didn’t seem inclined to press further either, focusing instead, with apparent disinterest, on brushing a Raph-species.
“Well… that cat there has had all sorts of aspects and the negative parts of worlds dumped onto it, you see. To put it in one phrase—not ‘Schrödinger’s cat,’ but more like ‘the box within the cat.’”
That sounded like a shortened version of something I’d heard before, I say. Schrödinger’s cat… the thought experiment, was it.

You put something with a fifty percent chance of killing it inside a box. Put the cat in, close the lid, and you don’t know whether it’s alive or dead—that one. Even I know that one, it’s famous enough.
“Isn’t it the reverse, though?”
“More or less. Whether the box inside the cat is open or closed, you can’t know without killing the cat and cutting it open to check. Whether what’s stored in that box is calamity or hope, you see.”
Ark furrowed his brow, looking mildly displeased.
“Are you trying to twist some famous concept about a certain cat into a smokescreen?”

“Nothing exists, yet it does. It doesn’t exist, yet it does. Being just as uncertain as that means it can also become a dumping ground that everyone unloads onto. I wonder where all that trash drifting through the void ends up going.”
“Space debris was a hot topic in my world too, come to think of it.”
“For every unit of energy produced, an equal amount of negative is born somewhere. Reaction, anti-existence… the world is forever fated to seek balance.”
“Really, you do talk a lot, don’t you.”
“Ehehe~”
Ark, looking exasperated at Ho-kun, carried on with that idle chatter.

That night. I went to the public bathhouse built in the village. Father had apparently already finished bathing and was sitting in a chair, fanning himself with a paper fan to cool off. What could he possibly be looking at through the window, I wondered?
“Raff.”
“Raph.”
“Tarry.”
“Reeah.”

The Raph-species had gathered beneath the moonlit night, drumming on their bellies and making a lively racket, and Father watched them with a smile. Hm… I noticed Chick too, gazing at that little festival alongside her Raph-species friends.
“…I wonder if Raphtalia wouldn’t want to join in and play with them too.”
Just then, with Big Sister apparently off bathing and nowhere nearby, Father murmured that quietly to himself. Truly, Father—there is nothing in this world he fears, I say.
